title: Additivity and well-definedness of the Euler defect on an integral proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\xi$ be its generic point, so $\overline{\{\xi\}}=C$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then $C$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $\mathcal O_{C,\xi}$ is a field canonically identified with $\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. For every coherent $\mathcal O_C$-module $\mathcal H$ [pqf-def-coherent], the tensor $\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal H$ is coherent [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the generic stalk $\mathcal H_\xi$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is finite-dimensional over $\kappa(\xi)$. Write $r(\mathcal H)=\dim_{\kappa(\xi)}\mathcal H_\xi$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and define the integer
$$D_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal H)=\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H)-\chi(C,\mathcal H)-r(\mathcal H)\deg_k(\mathcal L),$$
using Euler characteristic [def-pc-euler-characteristic] and degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Then $D_{\mathcal L}(0)=0$. For every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal H_1\to\mathcal H_2\to\mathcal H_3\to0$ of coherent modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] one has
$$r(\mathcal H_2)=r(\mathcal H_1)+r(\mathcal H_3),\qquad D_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal H_2)=D_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal H_1)+D_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal H_3).$$
In particular, the property $D_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal H)=0$ holds for the third term whenever it holds for any two terms of such a sequence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] with $Y=C$ and $\mathcal N=\mathcal L$: $C$ is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, and $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal O_C$ are coherent. The hypotheses are precisely properness over the field and invertibility; no smoothness or geometric integrality is required. Apply [lem-sc-rational-functions-generic-stalks] to the integral scheme $C$, which has just its one irreducible component, to see that $A=\mathcal O_{C,\xi}$ is a field. Its maximal ideal is zero (any nonzero element of an ideal in a field generates 1), so the quotient map $A\to A/0=\kappa(\xi)$ is a canonical isomorphism by [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tags 01T6 and 01RV, lemma-finite-type-noetherian and lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions; coherent.tex Tag 01XZ.

proof.text: For coherent $\mathcal H$, choose the open trivializations $\mathcal L|_U\cong\mathcal O_U$ of [def-sc-invertible-module]. On each such open, multiplication identifies $(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H)|_U$ with $\mathcal H|_U$: on presheaf pure tensors it sends $a\otimes h$ to $ah$, with inverse $h\mapsto1\otimes h$, and these inverse maps induce inverse maps after the sheafification in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus finite type and finite type of the kernels in the definition [pqf-def-coherent] hold locally for the tensor exactly as they do for $\mathcal H$. They hold on every open because finite type is local by that definition. Consequently $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H$ is coherent.

source.place: Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian; local rank-one tensor calculation spelled out.

proof.text: By finite type in [pqf-def-coherent], on some neighbourhood $U$ of $\xi$ there is a surjection $\mathcal O_U^m\to\mathcal H|_U$. Apply [def-sc-open-module-stalk-functor] on the scheme $U$ with its whole open and point $\xi$. Its finite-colimit preservation preserves the cokernel zero of this map, so it is a surjection on stalks. The stalk of a finite free sheaf is $A^m$: germs of a finite tuple give its tuple of germs, with inverse obtained by choosing representatives on the intersection of their finitely many neighbourhoods, as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Hence the $m$ standard germs span $\mathcal H_\xi$ over $A=\kappa(\xi)$. From a finite spanning list, delete each vector in the span of its predecessors; the resulting independent spanning list is a finite basis. Thus $r(\mathcal H)$ is finite.

source.place: Tags 01AG and 01AH, lemma-abelian and lemma-limits-colimits; finite type generators as in Tag 01B8, lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] to $\mathcal H$, $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H$, $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal O_C$, all coherent by steps 1–2 on the proper $k$-scheme $C$. Their Euler characteristics are integers. Therefore $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(C,\mathcal L)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$ by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] is an integer, and so is the displayed defect. For any coherent short exact sequence, [def-sc-open-module-stalk-functor] with $U=C$ preserves its kernels and cokernels and thus gives a short exact sequence of $A$-modules at $\xi$. Transport along the field quotient isomorphism of step 1 gives a short exact sequence of finite-dimensional $\kappa(\xi)$-vector spaces. Apply [lem-trf-finite-dimensional-short-exact-dimension] to obtain $r(\mathcal H_2)=r(\mathcal H_1)+r(\mathcal H_3)$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, condition (1); Tag 0AYR, definition-degree; preceding definition-euler-characteristic and its finiteness justification.

proof.text: An invertible module is finite locally free with local rank one by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Thus [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact] sends the given short exact sequence to $0\to\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H_1\to\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H_2\to\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H_3\to0$. Its terms are coherent by step 2. Apply [lem-pc-euler-additive] once to this sequence and once to the original one. Writing $a_i=\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H_i)$ and $b_i=\chi(C,\mathcal H_i)$, the results are $a_2=a_1+a_3$ and $b_2=b_1+b_3$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, proof of condition (1); Tag 08AA, lemma-euler-characteristic-additive.

proof.text: Put $d=\deg_k(\mathcal L)$ and $r_i=r(\mathcal H_i)$. Substitute the three preceding equalities and distribute multiplication in $\mathbf Z$: $D_{\mathcal L}(\mathcal H_2)=(a_1+a_3)-(b_1+b_3)-(r_1+r_3)d=(a_1-b_1-r_1d)+(a_3-b_3-r_3d)$. This proves defect additivity. The zero sheaf is coherent directly from [pqf-def-coherent] (its presentation has zero generators and a map from a finite free sheaf to zero has that finite free kernel). The stalk and tensor definitions give $0_\xi=0$ and $\mathcal L\otimes0=0$. Its dimension is zero, since its empty list is a basis [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Applying [lem-pc-euler-additive] to $0\to0\to0\to0\to0$ gives $\chi(C,0)=2\chi(C,0)$, hence $\chi(C,0)=0$ by subtraction in $\mathbf Z$. Thus $D_{\mathcal L}(0)=0$. Finally if $D_2=D_1+D_3$ and any two of the three integers vanish, solving that equality for the remaining integer gives zero.

lean.statement: theorem curve_euler_defect_additivity (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral C] [C.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper (C ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (ξ : C) (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Set.univ) (L : C.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] : IsLocallyNoetherian C ∧ CompactSpace C ∧ IsField (C.presheaf.stalk ξ) ∧ ∃ e : C.presheaf.stalk ξ ≃+* C.residueField ξ, e.toRingHom = (C.residue ξ).hom ∧ (∀ H : C.Modules, RingedSpace.IsCoherent C.toRingedSpace H → RingedSpace.IsCoherent C.toRingedSpace (L ⊗ H) ∧ FiniteDimensional (C.residueField ξ) (curveResidueStalk ξ e H)) ∧ curveEulerDefect k L ξ e (0 : C.Modules) = 0 ∧ (∀ S : ShortComplex C.Modules, S.ShortExact → RingedSpace.IsCoherent C.toRingedSpace S.X₁ → RingedSpace.IsCoherent C.toRingedSpace S.X₂ → RingedSpace.IsCoherent C.toRingedSpace S.X₃ → curveGenericRank ξ e S.X₂ = curveGenericRank ξ e S.X₁ + curveGenericRank ξ e S.X₃ ∧ curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₂ = curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₁ + curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₃ ∧ (curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₁ = 0 ∧ curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₂ = 0 → curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₃ = 0) ∧ (curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₁ = 0 ∧ curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₃ = 0 → curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₂ = 0) ∧ (curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₂ = 0 ∧ curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₃ = 0 → curveEulerDefect k L ξ e S.X₁ = 0))
lean.note: The generic stalk keeps its existing carrier and receives the residue-field action by restriction of scalars along the inverse of e. The theorem characterizes e as the canonical residue quotient, and asserts its existence and the field property as conclusions, not hypotheses. Added the already recorded def-pc-module-stalk-functor to cite the ringed-space stalk interface used on schemes. Helpers belong to the rank and defect notation introduced in this node; their data are explicit.
